summary.text: St. Nathan is the prophet who speaks God’s promise to St. David, confronts his sin and takes part in St. Solomon’s succession.

blocks.text: St. Nathan appears as a prophet in the royal court of St. David. In Second Samuel 7 he first responds to the king’s desire to build a house for God, then delivers a revelation concerning David’s house and enduring kingdom. He is the prophet, distinct from David’s son of the same name.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

sections.title: Confronting the king and securing succession

blocks.text: After the king’s adultery and the killing of the woman’s husband, Nathan tells a story about a rich man taking a poor man’s only lamb. He then identifies the king as the guilty man. David confesses, and Nathan announces God’s forgiveness while also declaring consequences. First Kings later records Nathan’s intervention when the royal succession is contested and his participation in Solomon’s anointing.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The biblical passages used here do not describe St. Nathan’s death. This profile therefore assigns no unsupported lifespan, burial site or martyrdom narrative.

blocks.text: The OCA names St. Nathan among the holy prophets and connects his encounter with St. David to the Church’s prayer of absolution in confession. His story is therefore relevant both to biblical kingship and to repentance.
